gradeNote: F10 A (decision 0272): every newly made piece rolls a maker's grade. `mul` scales its main effect and its extra effects, never its charms; `weight` is how often. The budget is a Fair piece's, so the grade is the only thing outside it. Masterwork never comes on Homespun.

reroll.note: Decision 0276: a tailor rolls one extra effect again for goods. The first costs what moving a charm costs on that tier (`unpick`); each one after on the same piece costs `growth` times the last, rounded up, rising `rises` times and then staying there (Matt, 8 Nov 2026: cap at 21 on a Stout piece).

extraNote: F10 B (decision 0272): each slot's extra effects. `lo` and `hi` are a Stout piece's range for `field`; a tier multiplies them by its `extraSize`, and the grade by its `mul`. `as`: more and less make `field` a multiplier (1 + size, 1 - size). `points` is the price of the middle of the Stout range, from tools/gear/sim/extrabench.mjs; a bigger size costs in proportion. Extras spend from the piece's budget, at most `extraShare` of what's left after its main effect. One of each `does` at most on a piece. A keepsake from Sunday Best up takes one from any slot's list.

regionNote: F10 D2 (decision 0396): each region's own extra effect, found nowhere else. A piece found in a region (from a fight, a chest, a merchant or a notice, wherever Eldwin stands) carries one at `chance`, if its slot is in `slots`. A place with its own list (the Deep Cut) uses it instead of its region's. It comes on top of the piece's budget, on every tier, sized like an extra (`lo`, `hi` times the tier's `extraSize`, then the grade). `points` from tools/gear/sim/extrabench.mjs (9 Nov 2026): Toll-paid was worth more than a whole Stout main effect at 30% softer, so it's 10 to 14%; the other three price at the floor. Woodswise (the Tanbark Road, decision 0428) is all or nothing, so its size changes nothing: measured at 0.16 of a level, it costs 2.1, about two Stout main effects. Re-rolls leave it alone.

growth.note: Grows with you (F10 D4, decision 0397): `fights` worn through at a tier before a tailor can raise the piece one tier, and `cost` in goods to raise it from that tier (half what a piece of the next tier is worth). Every fight counts, won or lost, for every piece worn by anyone who fought (Matt, 9 Nov 2026). Heirloom is the top; Old Work is only found.

any: The left one always did run tight
Somebody cared for it longer than anyone remembers
Traded twice at the same fair
Smells faintly of the last person's pipe
Won at a husking bee, or so the story went
Came out of a cellar hole with the cellar still on it
Left on a fence post one spring and never claimed
Mended with whatever was in the house that winter
The stitching is better than the cloth
Bought from a peddler who never came back through
Three families claim it was theirs
Kept in cedar, and it shows
Too good to wear, according to everybody who wore it
boots: Walked to the coast and back on one pair of soles
Greased every fall whether it needed it or not
Muddy from a road nobody can place
gloves: Worn through at the thumb by one particular job
Knit by someone who was counting under her breath
Too warm for the work, and the work got done anyway
coat: Turned once already, and it could stand turning again
Has a pocket that wasn't in the pattern
Hung behind one door for most of a lifetime
belt: Has been let out four notches and taken in two
Holds more than it looks like it should
The buckle came off something else
keepsake: Nobody can say what it opened or who it was for
Passed along at a graveside, the way they do
Found in a wall when the wall came down
Worn smooth where a thumb goes
